newsitem.title: INDIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 5.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indian newspapers - September 5.

text.p: Following is a summary of major Indian business and political stories in leading newspapers prepared for Reuters by Business News and Information Services Pvt Ltd, New Delhi. Telephone: 11-3324842, 11-3761233; Fax: 91-11-3351006 Internet : biznis.news@forums.sprintrpg.sprint.com
TOP STORIES
The Hindustan Times
FORMER PRIME MINISTER QUESTIONED IN PAY-OFF CASE

The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) interrogated former prime minister Narasimha Rao over his alleged role in the Jharkhand Mukti Morcha (JMM) pay-off case. Rao was queried about his role in bribing the four JMM Parliament members (MPs) to gain their support in a no-confidence vote on the floor of Parliament back in 1993. Rao is learnt to have denied having any knowledge of the payments made to JMM MPs. Questions about the sources of the money and the alleged role of other senior politicians were also denied by Rao.
The Times Of India
UNION GOVERNMENT RULES OUT PRESIDENT'S RULE IN GUJARAT

The Union government has ruled out any intervention in the ongoing political deadlock in Gujarat arising out of a split in the ruling Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP). A Home Ministry official denied any move to impose President's rule in Gujarat. The Ministry's response came in the wake of fears expressed by BJP that the United Front (UF) government was planning to dismiss the BJP government in Gujarat. The BJP government in the state faced a deadlock following the state deputy speaker's recognition of a breakaway faction of BJP. BJP had asked the President to direct the state's Governor to convene a session of the state Assembly for the BJP government to prove its majority.
Indian Express
USA LAUNCHES SECOND MISSILE STRIKE ON IRAQ

The U.S. warships in the Gulf launched a second missile strike against Iraqi military installations and its war planes went into action to enforce an expanded no-fly zone in southern Iraq. The UN Security Council has decided to continue the stiff economic sanctions imposed on Baghdad. Immediately after the second attack, the Iraqi President, Saddam Hussein presided over a meeting of the Revolutionary Command Council, the country's highest policy making body, and discussed details of US aggression and took a number of decisions in response to the missile attack. Russia, meanwhile, warned to veto a UN Security Council vote on action against Iraq.
Business Standard
FIRMS MAY BE TOLD TO PRUNE GDR OFFER, RAISE LOCAL FUNDS

Security and Exchange Board of India (SEBI), the bourse regulator, may request the Union finance ministry to direct corporates to earmark a part of their global depositary receipt (GDR) issues for the domestic capital market. This is part of a series of measures the bourse regulator plans to take for reviving the primary share market. This step, SEBI feels will ensure that some good issues, currently going overseas, come to the domestic equity market.
SOPS TO PEP UP CAPITAL MARKET LIKELY

The Finance Ministry is considering a series of sops to pep up the capital markets, including relaxation in dividend taxation norms and permission for stock lending. A review of the minimum alternate tax (MAT) on zero tax companies is also on the cards. Official sources said though MAT would not be withdrawn, the possibility of either a lower MAT rate or an exemption to certain categories of companies, like exporters, could not be ruled out. These measures, if cleared, are expected to considerably lift capital market sentiments.
UNIT TRUST'S MONEY MARKET MUTUAL CLEARED

Reserve Bank of India (RBI), the central bank, has cleared the Unit Trust of India (UTI)'s proposal to set up the country's first ever money market mutual fund (MMMF). The setting up of MMMF will add depth to the money market. MMMF will also act as a transmission mechanism through which individual investors can park funds in government securities. The details of MMMF being floated by UTI are still not available. UTI sources say the details will be worked out after the central bank formally clears the proposal. UTI is planning to tie up with UTI Bank under which the bank will manage the fund.
STOCKS STAGE RECOVERY

Equity prices recovered moderately on renewed buying support from foreign institutional investors (FIIs) and common investors on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE). The market opened with a dull note as the U.S. launched a fresh attack against Iraq. But towards the end of the trading session, the FIIs started purchasing blue chips. The BSE sensitive index rose to 3516.90 points against its previous close of 3484.68, showing a gain of 32.22 points. The BSE-100 also improved marginally, closing at 1578.33 against a previous close of 1576.20.
The Economic Times
RELIANCE CAPITAL TO RAKE IN 20 BLN RUPEES IN FIXED DEPOSITS

Reliance Capital, a Reliance group company, is going to offer interest rates as high as 20 percent for its forthcoming fixed deposit (FD) programme targeted to raise 20 billion rupees. The interest rates that Reliance Capital plans to offer are: 15 percent on one year, 16 percent on two, 18 percent on three, 19 percent on four and 20 percent on a five year FD. Reliance sources said the company decided to raise the interest rate on FDs following the central bank's decision to free the interest rates on deposits raised by the non banking finance companies.
HOT FUNDS MAY ELUDE TELECOMMUNICATION SECTOR

Telecommunication ventures in the country may face a dearth of funds from external sources in the near future. The ongoing telecommunication scandal is scaring foreign investors away from investing in Indian services companies. The Union finance ministry is learnt to be doubtful about being able to disburse the bulk of $1.5 billion earmarked for external commercial borrowings for this sector. In the next three to five years, the requirement of external funds for the telecommunication services sector is pegged at $20 billion.
GVK PROJECT GETS COUNTER GUARANTEE

The Union government signed the counter guarantee agreement with GVK Industries for the 216 MW Jegurupadu power project in Andhra Pradesh. Sources said a tripartite agreement between the Union government, Andhra Pradesh and the Reserve Bank of India was also signed. Jegurupadu power project is the second project after Enron Corporation's Dabhol power project to receive a counter guarantee.
Financial Express
TWO TISCO-PROMOTED COMPANIES TO BE WOUND UP

Tata Steel may soon hive off two of the 11 companies promoted by it. The reason seems to be the fact of these companies having turned terminally sick. The companies that have turned sick include: Indian Steel Rolling Mills Ltd, Kumardubhi Metals Castings & Engineering Ltd, Tata Construction and Kalinga Aquatics Ltd. Tata Construction had a loss of 24.4 million rupees in 1995/96 and Indian Steel a loss of 67.5 million rupees in 1994/95. Kumardubhi Metals incurred a loss of 23.9 million rupees in 1994/95 and Kalinga Aquatics 42.6 million rupees in 1994/95.
NEW EXPORT-IMPORT POLICY ON ANVIL

The government is working on a five-year export-import policy with emphasis on the promotion of high value added branded products in the export market and drastic reduction of paper work. The India Brand Equity Fund would be activated and the corpus raised to five billion rupees to promote the Made-in-India label. Initiating the exercise for formulation of the new policy, the Commerce Ministry has invited suggestions from trade and industry at the Board of Trade meeting on August 13.
SONY TO SET UP UNIT UNDER INDIAN ARM

The $45-billion Japanese multinational Sony Corporation is planning to enter the Indian computer software market in a big way. It is planning to set up an independent unit under its wholly-owned subsidiary, Sony India Pvt Ltd, for the purpose. Initially, the production of software from the Indian unit would be outsourced to Sony's two main overseas operations, sony America and Sony Europe. Besides this, Sony would also be expanding the range of colour televisions which it has been manufacturing in India since it set up shop in 1995.
The Observer
GOVERNMENT APATHY HALTS OIL, GAS EXPLORATION

Exploration of hydrocarbon in the country has come to a grinding halt due to high finance costs involved. The reason being government's lukewarm response to private sector participation in this sector. These two factors have forced the domestic as well as the foreign oil companies during the past few months to opt out of the government's present hydrocarbon exploration activities. Industry sources said this was evident from the fact that the country could explore only six basins, as against 26 identified basins where oil and gas could be struck.
PRIME LENDING RATE MAY DECLINE TO 15 PCT

The prime lending rate may decline to around 15 percent prior to the start of the busy season credit policy in October. According to Indian Bank Association sources, lack of demand for credit, combined with various constraints being faced by the banks, is leading towards this inevitable decline. The lending rate for most creditworthy borrowers, which had been pegged at 16.5 percent was recently brought down to 16 percent.
Business Line
OIL MINISTRY PLANS CONTINGENCY STRATEGY

The Union petroleum ministry held top-level meetings to assess the impact of the global spurt in oil prices on India, at the aftermath of U.S. missile strike on Iraq. The ministry is said to be formulating a contingency strategy to deal with a scenario of sustained high oil prices. Sources in the ministry revealed that an increase of one dollar a barrel in the price of crude could raise the annual burden on the oil pool account by 12 billion rupees. Oil Co-ordination Committee officials are learnt to be evaluating the impact of the global price rise on the oil import bill. The oil ministry, however, does not envisage a any disruption in the supply of oil.
